source.title: Complete intersection liaison and Gorenstein liaison: new results and open problems

accepted.question_text: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let R = k[X0, ..., X_{n+3}] with irrelevant maximal ideal m, and let X be a closed arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subscheme of P^{n+3} of dimension n > 0 and codimension 3. Let I = I(X), A = R/I, and K = Ext^3_R(A,R)(-n-4), the canonical module of X. A necessary condition for X to be licci is that the local cohomology groups H^i_m(K tensor_R I) vanish for all 0 <= i <= n. Is the converse true: whenever H^i_m(K tensor_R I) = 0 for every i with 0 <= i <= n, must X be licci, meaning in the complete-intersection liaison class of a complete intersection?

Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and consider arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subschemes X of projective space P^n of fixed codimension c. Two equidimensional schemes without embedded components are in the same Gorenstein liaison class when they can be connected by a sequence of direct Gorenstein links through arithmetically Gorenstein schemes; a scheme is glicci when it lies in the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection. Is there only one Gorenstein liaison class containing all arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay subschemes of P^n of codimension c, equivalently are all such subschemes glicci?
accepted.context_brief: ACM schemes and Gorenstein liaison classes

evidence.quote: are all ACM subschemes X ⊂ Pn glicci?

accepted.question_text: Let C_t be an arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curve in P^n whose homogeneous ideal I(C_t) has the t-linear free resolution 0 -> R(-t-2)^((t^2+t)/2) -> R(-t-1)^(t^2+2t) -> R(-t)^((t^2+3t+2)/2) -> I(C_t) -> 0 over the homogeneous coordinate ring R. Is every such curve C_t glicci, meaning in the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection?

evidence.quote: Is any ACM curve Ct ⊂ Pn

accepted.question_text: Let X_{p,q,r} be a subscheme of P^n defined by the r by r minors of a p by q homogeneous matrix, where r <= min(p,q). Assume X_{p,q,r} has the expected codimension codim(X_{p,q,r}) = (p-r+1)(q-r+1), and is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay. Is X_{p,q,r} in the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection, i.e. is X_{p,q,r} glicci?
accepted.context_brief: Determinantal schemes from r by r minors

trace.notes: Normalized the single input URL as a zbMATH resolver record. Local workflow metadata for zbMATH id 2217233 identified the exact title, year, source family, and problem-tagged status.

The zbMATH landing page was treated as a bibliographic resolver. Exact-title recovery found the Le Matematiche article page and its direct PDF, matching the title, author, journal issue, and page range for the same work. The direct PDF was selected as the readable primary source.

Mapped the 19-page PDF. Section 1 introduces the comparison between complete-intersection liaison and Gorenstein liaison. Section 2 gives the definitions of direct links, liaison classes, licci, and glicci. Section 3 develops complete-intersection liaison invariants and the local cohomology obstruction used later. Section 4 lists positive glicci results for ACM curves and divisors. Section 5 proves the standard determinantal generalization of Gaeta's theorem. Section 6 is the explicit further-comments and questions region.
Section 1 contains broad motivation about higher-codimension open questions but no standalone extractable research question beyond the later explicit question section.
Section 2 supplies definitions and examples for CI-liaison, G-liaison, licci, and glicci; it does not formulate a separate open problem.
Section 3 states invariants, criteria, and examples distinguishing complete-intersection liaison classes. No open problem candidate was accepted from this section.
Section 4 presents positive glicci results for ACM curves and divisors on specified surfaces; no standalone open question is posed there.

Section 5 states and sketches the standard determinantal generalization of Gaeta's theorem. The section motivates the later broad determinantal-minors question but does not itself pose an additional candidate.

Extracted four explicit candidates: the codimension-3 licci converse question; the single Gorenstein liaison class/all-ACM-glicci question; the t-linear-resolution ACM curve glicci question; and the expected-codimension determinantal-minors glicci question. The closing non-ACM paragraph was treated as contextual because it does not state a self-contained unresolved problem.
